title: A comparison of soft palate thickness, length, and volume in bulldogs before and after staphylectomy or folded-flap palatoplasty: A prospective clinical study
content:
by Eva A. Ruzics, Cristina Piedrahita Velasquez, Penny J. Regier, Diego A. Portela, Kathleen M. Ham, James Colee, Federico R. Vilaplana Grosso

Objectives

To compare soft palate (SP) length, thickness, and volume in French bulldogs and English bulldogs before and after staphylectomy or folded flap palatoplasty (FFP), and to compare the success of procedures in reducing these dimensions.

Materials and Methods

Dogs diagnosed with brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) underwent staphylectomy (n = 8) or FFP (n = 8). Pre-operative and 4-week post-operative computed tomography was performed to assess SP dimensions and evaluate surgical outcomes.

Results

Both procedures resulted in a reduction of SP length (staphylectomy mean reduction = 0.91 cm, 95% CI [0.44 cm, 1.39 cm]; FFP mean reduction = 0.86 cm, 95% CI [0.39 cm, 1.33 cm]), and volume (staphylectomy mean reduction = 2.81 cm3, 95% CI [1.36 cm3, 4.27 cm3]; FFP mean reduction = 2.54 cm3, 95% CI [0.84 cm3, 4.24 cm3]) when comparing pre- and post-operative dimensions within each procedure group. Staphylectomy did not result in SP thinning, while FFP resulted in a mean thinning of 0.30 cm (95% CI [0.10 cm, 0.50 cm]). There was no difference in the degree of SP shortening (adjusted mean difference 0.01 cm, 95% CI [−0.33 cm, 0.35] cm) or reduction of SP volume (adjusted mean difference 0.32 cm3, 95% CI [−0.52 cm3, 1.16 cm3]) between procedure groups. Folded flap palatoplasty resulted in greater SP thinning than staphylectomy.

Clinical Significance

Both staphylectomy and FFP resulted in a reduction of length and volume of the SP. FFP resulted in SP thinning, while staphylectomy did not. In dogs with concurrent SP thickening and elongation, FFP may be the preferred surgical treatment.
